To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the dominant interaction between two stressors (predator and calcium concentration) was synergistic; 2) this synergistic interaction resulted in changes in expression patterns of genes that play a role in calcium homeostatic mechanisms; and 3) these changes were not additive, and were nonlinear, yet dose-dependent across the calcium gradient.
